fieldMarks: Coarse yellow-brown to tawny upper pelage, often frosted, with a buffy band on the side of the neck
Whitish band across the snout in most
Short bushy tail; total length up to about 68 cm (ADW: 470-700 mm)
behavior: Whistles to signal alarm, plus scream and tooth chatter
Lives alone, in pairs or colonies with territorial males, 1-5 adult females and young
Hibernates early September to May at higher elevations; may emerge February-March lower down
Generalist herbivore: grasses and forbs; does not store food
habitat: Alpine tundra, subalpine and montane meadows, foothills and canyons; semifossorial, burrowing under rocks in talus, outcrops or boulder fields.
range: South-central British Columbia and southern Alberta south to southern California, Nevada, southern Utah and northern New Mexico, typically above 2,000 m.
